title: Fill Date Gaps Using GENERATE_SERIES
description:
Generate every day in the week 2026-01-01 through 2026-01-07 and show total sales for each day (0 if there were no sales that day).

**Table: daily_sales** — `sale_date`, `amount`

Output columns: `day_date`, `total_sales`. Order by `day_date`.
solution_sql: SELECT t.day_date, COALESCE(SUM(s.amount), 0) AS total_sales FROM generate_series(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-01-07', INTERVAL '1 day') AS t(day_date) LEFT JOIN daily_sales s ON s.sale_date = t.day_date GROUP BY t.day_date ORDER BY t.day_date

test_cases.description: 7 days generated; Jan 3 and Jan 6 have no sales so total_sales=0 for those days

hints: generate_series(start, stop, step) creates a virtual table of dates — LEFT JOIN it with your data table to fill gaps.
Wrap the sum in COALESCE(..., 0) so that days with no matching sales rows show 0 instead of NULL.
explanation: generate_series produces all 7 dates. LEFT JOIN daily_sales keeps all 7 rows even when there is no matching sale. Jan 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 have sales; Jan 3 and Jan 6 get NULL from the LEFT JOIN which COALESCE converts to 0. GROUP BY day_date collapses any multi-row days (none here) and SUM aggregates them.
